> RoboCore X1 is a custom PCB designed to act as the main control board for a small robotics project. It will connect a microcontroller to motors, sensors, servos, buttons, and other components while keeping the wiring organized. The goal is to create a reusable board that can control and monitor different robotic systems.

## Design

### 2026-10-10 – I started working on RoboCore X1, a custom robotics control board that I plan to design as part of my Hack Club Half Life project. The goal is to create a reusable PCB that can connect a microcontroll

**2h**

I started working on RoboCore X1, a custom robotics control board that I plan to design as part of my Hack Club Half Life project. The goal is to create a reusable PCB that can connect a microcontroller to motors, servos, sensors, and other components used in robotics projects.

I installed KiCad, which I will use to design the circuit schematic and PCB layout.

### 2026-10-11 – During my first week, I focused on designing RoboCore X1, a robotics controller expansion board built around the XIAO ESP32-C3 microcontroller. The goal was to create a board that could connect sensor

**15h**

During my first week, I focused on designing RoboCore X1, a robotics controller expansion board built around the XIAO ESP32-C3 microcontroller. The goal was to create a board that could connect sensors and external motor-driver modules while keeping the wiring organized.

I started by setting up KiCad and learning how to use its Schematic Editor. I added connector symbols, resistors, and an LED to begin planning the circuit. I also researched the XIAO ESP32-C3 pinout to understand how the controller could connect to different components.

Next, I developed the schematic design, planning connections for power input, power output, two sensor ports, an external motor-driver port, and a status LED. I then created a visual reference for the intended schematic to help organize the circuit.
